directionGuardrail: Historical prototype. Current direction packages original Grey Crow; most world material is saved as Skill/Memory/World records, while Hard Commit Validator only protects narrow app/UI state.
globalRules: Skill rewrites describe runtime capability boundaries; they are not OpenClaw Markdown skills.
Model-visible skills can read context and write controlled saveRoot records through current domain tools.
Runtime-only lifecycle skills can write narrow app/UI state or save metadata, but the model cannot call them.
Candidate is not fact; narration is not state; memory is not authority.
No API key, provider raw body, local filesystem path, prompt text, or raw tool trace can appear in skill output.
No image generation, scene visualizer, portrait generation, image relay, OpenClaw Gateway, shell, or arbitrary file access.

skills.name: read_map
skills.purpose: Read confirmed world, location, exit, nearby point, and route-constraint facts without moving the player.

properties.location: optional string; if omitted, runtime uses State Store scene.location
properties.query: optional string for place, route, exit, or point-of-interest lookup
properties.scope: optional enum: current_location | nearby | route | known_world

forbidden: player-provided new location as confirmed fact
movement intent disguised as a read

requirements: Every returned place, exit, and route constraint must be confirmed, unknown, or not_found.
Unknown routes stay unknown instead of being invented.
Output cannot include local paths, hidden implementation details, or raw store records.

factGateRequirements: New points of interest from narration become candidate_events only.
Movement must be proposed through propose_event and validated before State Store changes.
Contradictions with current State Store or World Fact Store must be returned as unknowns.
implementationNotes: P2-04A defines the executable contract and registers a minimal read_map executor.
engine/runtime/world-map-store.js reads confirmed per-save world-map.json data when present.
If no world map data exists, read_map returns a State Store current-location fallback with unknown routes.

skills.name: new_game_init
skills.purpose: Create a desktop save slot and initialize the first confirmed State Store snapshot from a runtime-owned template.

properties.title: optional player-visible save title
properties.providerStatus: runtime-owned readiness flag; never contains the API key
properties.overwriteSaveId: optional save id only after explicit UI confirmation

forbidden: raw player backstory promoted directly into facts
local dataRoot or save directory path

requirements: Output is safe for renderer display.
State hint is a projection, not the full state.
No local path and no credential metadata.

factGateRequirements: Initial state comes from a checked runtime template.
Player-authored setup text is candidate material until validated.
Host Profile can influence tone only, not initial facts.
Session credential readiness can unlock new game flow but never enters State Store.
implementationNotes: Desktop main process owns save slot creation.
The renderer can request new game only through the desktop bridge path.
engine/bridge/desktop-bridge.js exposes initializeNewGame only to Desktop main, not to the renderer or model tools.
engine/runtime/state-store.js writes the runtime-owned initial state snapshot before the first player turn.
P2-04C aligned save_lifecycle with rename, delete, overwrite confirmation, and snapshot marker behavior.

skills.name: save_lifecycle
skills.purpose: Own save listing, creation, rename, overwrite, delete confirmation, restore selection, and renderer-safe summary projection.

properties.operation: list | create | rename | restore | snapshot | overwrite | delete
properties.title: optional renderer-provided title for rename/create

forbidden: raw full state returned to renderer

requirements: Delete and overwrite require explicit UI confirmation.
Current overwrite executor remains disabled until a replacement source exists.
Errors must be path-free and secret-free.
Current Demo does not expose Restore; if future Restore is reintroduced, it must return only a selected save identity and state hint, not raw files.

factGateRequirements: Save metadata changes are runtime lifecycle changes, not model facts.
Snapshot writes must happen after Runtime has committed accepted events.
Deleting a save must not be representable as a model tool call.
Overwrite cannot reuse player narration as confirmation.
implementationNotes: P2-01C already created list/create/get save-slot primitives.
P2-04C adds rename, restore, snapshot marker, delete confirmation, and overwrite confirmation contract in apps/desktop/electron/save-slots.js.
Delete is executable only after a runtime-issued confirmation token.
Overwrite is confirmation-gated but intentionally reserved until a concrete replacement source and UI flow exist.
Future Keychain or credential storage must remain outside save lifecycle data.

skills.name: memory_fragment
skills.purpose: Retrieve audit-safe memory fragments as narrative context while preserving State Store and Hard Commit Validator authority.

forbidden: request to treat memory as confirmed fact

requirements: Every memory result must be marked not_fact or historical_context.
Memory note text cannot directly overwrite State Store.
Accepted event summaries remain summaries, not new facts.

factGateRequirements: Memory can motivate a candidate event, but Hard Commit Validator must validate hard state before commit.
Contradictions between memory and current state resolve in favor of State Store.
Compacted memory must retain state anchors and source ranges.
implementationNotes: search_memory stays model-visible.
append_memory and compact_context stay runtime-only.
This replaces old memory-fragment prose with explicit authority tags.

skills.name: camp
skills.purpose: Potential future rest, shelter, resource, and long-term safety loop. It is not part of the current demo loop.
factGateRequirements: Camp cannot create supplies, shelter, safety, or recovery without explicit confirmed inputs.
Rest or resource changes must have costs and State Store projections.
Camp should not be introduced as ambient narration before its state fields exist.
implementationNotes: Do not expose camp as a tool in P2-04A.
Do not add camp to the context assembler until the domain schema is defined.
P2-04D adds deferred-skills-boundary smoke coverage so camp stays out of Tool Registry, Tool Router, and runtime context until its domain schema exists.
This keeps player imagination focused on the core Grey Crow runtime instead of adding a side system too early.
